instructions.humanOwned: Fill only semantics properties. Null, empty arrays, and empty objects are intentional blanks.
instructions.compilerOwned: The compiler refreshes mechanics and database metadata and preserves semantics during synchronization.
instructions.authority: The database is authoritative for mechanics. This file is the sole authority for human meaning.

semantics.purpose: Associates any observable activity event with all files that were supplied to it or produced by it.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row links one stored file to one activity event in a specific ordered role.
importantRules: Use activity_events.primary_file_id only for the one primary file; this relationship preserves every associated file.
semantics.sensitivity: Links private files to private interactions and observable agent operations.

semantics.meaning: Observable activity event to which the file belongs.
Stored-file record associated with the activity event.
How the file participates in the activity event.

allowedValueMeanings.attachment: File attached to a user request or other event.
allowedValueMeanings.input: File consumed as an explicit operation input.
allowedValueMeanings.other: File relationship not covered by the named roles.

semantics.meaning: Zero-based display and processing order among files associated with the event.
Connects this event-file association to its observable activity event.
semantics.cardinality: Each association references exactly one activity event; one event may have many associated files.
importantRules: Deleting the event also deletes this association, not the stored file itself.

semantics.meaning: Connects this event-file association to its stored-file record.
semantics.cardinality: Each association references exactly one stored file; one file may be associated with many events.
importantRules: Deleting the stored-file record also deletes this association.

semantics.purpose: Preserves a chronological, searchable record of activity visible at the boundaries between users, agents, models, tools, services, and external systems.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one observed event, such as a request arriving, a model call starting, a tool returning a result, a response being produced, or an error occurring.
importantRules: Treat rows as append-oriented historical evidence; corrections should normally be recorded as later events rather than rewriting prior observations.
Use event_seq for exact local insertion order and occurred_at_ms for source-event chronology.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private user content, tool arguments, model-visible data, errors, and operational identifiers.

semantics.meaning: Monotonically increasing local sequence used to order ledger insertions exactly.
Stable public identifier used to refer to this event from other records and interfaces.
When the represented event occurred according to its source, expressed as Unix epoch milliseconds.
When this ledger received and stored the event, expressed as Unix epoch milliseconds.
Human-readable UTC timestamp corresponding to the event occurrence time recorded for this row.
Extensible event name identifying what happened, such as a request, model call, tool call, response, lifecycle transition, or error.
Whether this record is a standalone point event or the start, successful end, or error end of an operation.

allowedValueMeanings.point: Standalone event rather than an operation boundary.
allowedValueMeanings.end: Operation completed without a recorded error.

semantics.meaning: Optional source-specific state or outcome associated with the event.
Broad category of the participant or system component that performed the recorded action.
More specific human-readable or machine-readable identity of the actor when known.
System, plugin, service, or integration that supplied the event to the ledger.
Communication channel through which the event entered or left the agent system, when applicable.
Identifier grouping events belonging to the same agent runtime session.
Identifier grouping all observable events belonging to one user-request and assistant-response turn.
Identifier grouping a distributed chain of related operations across components.
Identifier pairing the start and terminal events for one measurable operation.
Identifier of this event's tracing span when span-level tracing is available.
Identifier of the tracing span that directly contains this span.
Stable event_id of the earlier ledger event that directly caused or contains this event when known.
Short human-readable operation, event, model, tool, or component name.
Complete human-readable content visible at this event boundary, such as a user request, transcript, model output, or tool text.
Structured event-specific details, including observable arguments, results, identifiers, usage, or provider metadata not represented by dedicated columns.
File record most directly associated with this event, such as its original recording or generated artifact.
Type of domain record this event concerns, used together with subject_id.
Identifier of the domain record named by subject_type.
Identifier or reference assigned by an external system when no dedicated column exists.
Complete observable error message or terminal failure text associated with this event.
Connects this observable event to the stored-file record identified by primary_file_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each observable event may reference zero or one stored-file record; one referenced record may be used by many observable event records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

mechanics.definition: with operation_times as (select `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`operation_id` AS `operation_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`trace_id` AS `trace_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`name` AS `name`,min(case when `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_phase` = 'start' then `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms` end) AS `started_at_ms`,max(case when `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_phase` in ('end','error') then `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms` end) AS `finished_at_ms`,max(case when `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_phase` = 'error' then 1 else 0 end) AS `ended_in_error` from `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events` where `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`operation_id` is not null group by `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`operation_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`trace_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`name`)select `operation_times`.`operation_id` AS `operation_id`,`operation_times`.`trace_id` AS `trace_id`,`operation_times`.`name` AS `name`,`operation_times`.`started_at_ms` AS `started_at_ms`,`operation_times`.`finished_at_ms` AS `finished_at_ms`,case when `operation_times`.`started_at_ms` is not null and `operation_times`.`finished_at_ms` is not null then `operation_times`.`finished_at_ms` - `operation_times`.`started_at_ms` end AS `duration_ms`,`operation_times`.`ended_in_error` AS `ended_in_error` from `operation_times`

semantics.purpose: Summarizes elapsed time and error completion for operations reconstructed from their activity_events start, end, and error records.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row summarizes one operation_id, using its earliest start and latest end or error event.
importantRules: A null duration means the ledger does not contain both a start and a terminal event for the operation.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains operational identifiers and names derived from the private activity ledger.

semantics.meaning: Earliest recorded start-event time for the operation, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
Latest recorded end- or error-event time for the operation, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
Elapsed milliseconds between started_at_ms and finished_at_ms; null when either boundary is missing.
Derived 1 when any grouped event has error phase, otherwise 0.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_seq` AS `event_seq`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_id` AS `event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms` AS `occurred_at_ms`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`recorded_at_ms` AS `recorded_at_ms`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_utc` AS `occurred_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_type` AS `event_type`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_phase` AS `event_phase`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`status` AS `status`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`actor_type` AS `actor_type`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`actor_name` AS `actor_name`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`source` AS `source`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`channel` AS `channel`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`session_id` AS `session_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`turn_id` AS `turn_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`trace_id` AS `trace_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`operation_id` AS `operation_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`span_id` AS `span_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`parent_span_id` AS `parent_span_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`parent_event_id` AS `parent_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`name` AS `name`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`content_text` AS `content_text`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`payload_json` AS `payload_json`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`primary_file_id` AS `primary_file_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`subject_type` AS `subject_type`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`subject_id` AS `subject_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`external_ref` AS `external_ref`,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`error_text` AS `error_text` from `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events` order by `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms` desc,`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_seq` desc limit 1000

semantics.purpose: Provides a convenient window containing the 1,000 most recent activity_events by source-event time and local sequence.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row is one activity_events record included in the current recent-event window.
importantRules: This view is bounded to 1,000 rows and therefore must not be treated as complete history.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the same private content and operational metadata as activity_events.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`turn_id` AS `turn_id`,min(`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms`) AS `started_at_ms`,max(`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms`) AS `finished_at_ms`,max(`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms`) - min(`chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`occurred_at_ms`) AS `duration_ms`,count(0) AS `event_count`,sum(case when `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`event_phase` = 'error' then 1 else 0 end) AS `error_count` from `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events` where `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`turn_id` is not null group by `chapeauxfous`.`activity_events`.`turn_id`

semantics.purpose: Summarizes the observed time span, event volume, and error count for each agent turn represented in activity_events.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row summarizes all ledger events carrying the same non-null turn_id.
keywords: how long did the agent take
importantRules: Duration is the difference between the earliest and latest observed event, not necessarily provider-reported model latency.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains agent-turn identifiers and operational measurements.

semantics.meaning: Earliest observed event time in the turn, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
Latest observed event time in the turn, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
Observed milliseconds between the first and last ledger event in the turn.
Number of activity_events records associated with the turn.
Number of turn events whose event_phase is error.

semantics.purpose: Retains attempt-correlation records created by the previous runtime; the standalone Agent Slayer runtime does not write this table.
semantics.rowMeaning: One legacy row associates a user-facing request with one attempt made by the previous runtime.
importantRules: Treat this table as retained historical compatibility data, not the current request execution path.
Current model and tool boundaries are recorded directly in activity_events.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains request hashes and internal run, session, and operation identifiers.

semantics.meaning: Stable identifier for this processing attempt.
Ledger event containing the original user-facing request that this attempt processes.
Type of user-facing request record being processed, such as a voice request.
Identifier of the user-facing request record named by subject_type.
One-based retry number within the same subject_type and subject_id.
the previous runtime session in which this attempt was submitted, when known.
Unique voice-service operation identifier used to correlate this attempt with ledger events.
the previous runtime run identifier confirmed for this attempt after correlation.
SHA-256 hash of the exact submitted request text used for deterministic prompt correlation.
Evidence used to associate the attempt with openclaw_run_id.

allowedValueMeanings.prompt_sha256: Matched by the SHA-256 hash of the exact submitted prompt.
allowedValueMeanings.gateway_result: Confirmed by the run identifier returned by the Gateway.

semantics.meaning: Current processing outcome of this attempt.

allowedValueMeanings.complete: Attempt produced its terminal response successfully.
allowedValueMeanings.interrupted: Processing stopped before a normal terminal result.

semantics.meaning: When processing began, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
When the the previous runtime run was associated with this attempt, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
When processing reached a terminal state, in Unix epoch milliseconds.
UTC timestamp when the attempt record was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to the attempt.
Connects this agent processing attempt to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each agent processing attempt references exactly one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many agent processing attempt records.
importantRules: The referenced row cannot be deleted while this row depends on it.

semantics.purpose: Associates contacts with calendar events while preserving each contact's participant role and response.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row states that one contact participates in one calendar event in one specific role.
importantRules: The same contact may appear more than once on an event only when the participant role differs.
semantics.sensitivity: May reveal a person's schedule, attendance, and relationship to an event.

semantics.meaning: Calendar event in which the contact participates.
Contact participating in the calendar event.
Role the contact has in the event.

allowedValueMeanings.organizer: Contact organizes or owns the event.
allowedValueMeanings.customer: Contact participates as the customer associated with the event.
allowedValueMeanings.other: A meaningful participant role not covered by the named values.

semantics.meaning: Provider or user response such as accepted, declined, tentative, or needs action when known.
Connects this calendar participant assignment to the contact identified by contact_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each calendar participant assignment references exactly one contact; one referenced record may be used by many calendar participant assignment records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.meaning: Connects this calendar participant assignment to the calendar event identified by calendar_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each calendar participant assignment references exactly one calendar event; one referenced record may be used by many calendar participant assignment records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.purpose: Records individual recurrence instances omitted from a repeating calendar event.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row excludes one generated occurrence from one recurring calendar event.
importantRules: A recurring event may have any number of excluded occurrences; never collapse them into one delimited or JSON field.
Values are normalized UTC instants used when expanding the parent event's recurrence rule.
semantics.sensitivity: Reveals changes and omissions in the user's private schedule.

semantics.meaning: Recurring calendar event whose generated occurrence is omitted.
importantRules: The referenced event supplies the recurrence rule.

semantics.meaning: UTC start instant of the recurrence instance that must not be generated or displayed.
Each exclusion belongs to exactly one recurring calendar event; an event may own many exclusions.
semantics.cardinality: many-to-one
importantRules: Deleting the parent event deletes its exclusions.

semantics.purpose: Stores every commitment and scheduled event in the user's one authoritative agent calendar.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one scheduled event or one materialized occurrence of a repeating event.
importantRules: starts_at_utc and ends_at_utc are UTC instants; time_zone preserves the intended display zone.
There is exactly one logical calendar; imported identifiers prevent duplicate events but never partition events into separate calendars.
Materialized repeating occurrences are ordinary event rows and may be edited independently.
planning_prompt_text is optional and records the exact proactive planning question associated with the scheduled time.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the user's private schedule, locations, participants, and imported calendar identifiers.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this calendar event.
Persistent iCalendar UID used to identify an imported event or recurrence family and prevent duplicate imports.
importantRules: This identifies imported calendar data; it does not identify a separate calendar.

semantics.meaning: Original iCalendar recurrence-instance identifier distinguishing this materialized occurrence within the shared UID.
importantRules: Together with ical_uid, this value prevents duplicate imports of the same recurring occurrence.

semantics.meaning: Human-readable event name shown on the calendar.
Complete available description or notes for the event.
Human-readable physical, virtual, or meeting location.
UTC instant when the event starts.
UTC instant when the event ends, when an end is known.
IANA or provider time-zone name used to display the event in its intended local time.
1 when the event represents a calendar day rather than a precise time; otherwise 0.
Current scheduling state of the event.

allowedValueMeanings.tentative: Event is proposed but not firmly confirmed.

importantRules: Calendar events happen; completion is represented only by the passage of time, not a stored event status.

semantics.meaning: iCalendar RRULE describing how the event repeats.
Ledger event that caused this calendar record to be created when known.
UTC timestamp when this local calendar record was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to this local calendar record.
Optional question the agent should proactively ask to help the user decide how this scheduled time will be used.
examples: What should we do during these four hours with the kids?
importantRules: Null means no proactive planning question is attached to this event.

semantics.meaning: Generated iCalendar UID used only for a non-recurring imported event so that the same single event cannot be stored twice.
semantics.format: Binary SHA-independent copy of ical_uid; null for recurrence instances
importantRules: Compiler-owned generated value used by calendar_events_ical_single; applications must not write it.

semantics.meaning: Connects this calendar event to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each calendar event may reference zero or one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many calendar event records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.purpose: Stores the email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, handles, URLs, and other reachable identities belonging to contacts.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one original contact value of one kind for one contact, plus matching and delivery metadata.
importantRules: value preserves the original representation; normalized_value exists for matching and lookup.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains personal contact information and delivery addresses.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this contact method.
Contact that owns this address or reachable identity.
Kind of address or identity stored in value.

allowedValueMeanings.other: Contact identity not covered by the named kinds.

semantics.meaning: Human-facing qualifier such as home, work, mobile, or billing.
Original address, number, handle, URL, or other contact value as supplied.
Canonicalized representation used for reliable lookup and matching while value preserves the original.
1 when this is the preferred contact method of its kind for the contact; otherwise 0.
1 when the agent may use this method as a delivery destination; otherwise 0.
UTC timestamp when this contact method was inserted.
Generated SHA-256 digest of the original contact value used to enforce uniqueness even when the value is too long to index directly.
importantRules: Compiler-owned generated value; applications must not write it.
semantics.sensitivity: A deterministic digest of personal contact information.

semantics.meaning: Connects this contact method to the contact identified by contact_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each contact method references exactly one contact; one referenced record may be used by many contact method records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.purpose: Provides one address book for people, organizations, and services that other agent records need to identify or relate to.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one person, organization, or service known to the user.
importantRules: At most one active contact may have is_self set to 1.
Use contact_methods for reachable addresses rather than placing them in notes.
birth_date is the authoritative birthday fact; calendar birthday entries are derived from it.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains personal identity, birth dates, relationship, status, and free-text notes.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this person, organization, or service.
Whether this contact represents a person, organization, or service identity.

allowedValueMeanings.organization: Company, group, agency, or other organization.
allowedValueMeanings.service: Service or system represented as a contactable identity.

semantics.meaning: Preferred human-readable name used to show and refer to the contact.
Person's given or first name when the contact is a person.
Person's family or last name when the contact is a person.
Organization name associated with this contact when applicable.
1 only for the active contact record representing the user; otherwise 0.
Current address-book status of the contact.

allowedValueMeanings.blocked: Contact from whom interaction is blocked or should be avoided.
allowedValueMeanings.deceased: Person is known to be deceased.

semantics.meaning: Private free-text context about the contact that does not belong in a structured relationship or method.
System or process from which this contact was imported or created.
Identifier assigned to this contact by the source system.
UTC timestamp when the contact record was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to the contact.
Contact's birth date, with an explicitly optional year, used to derive birthday calendar entries and age when possible.
semantics.format: YYYY-MM-DD when the year is known; --MM-DD when it is unknown
importantRules: Do not invent a birth year; use --MM-DD when only month and day are known.
Age is derived only when the stored value includes a year.
Generated birthday labels are projections and must not be written back as permanent age text.
semantics.sensitivity: A birth date tied to an identified person is sensitive personal information.

semantics.meaning: Generated uniqueness guard equal to 1 only for the active contact representing the user, and null otherwise.
semantics.format: MariaDB boolean uniqueness guard: 1 or null
importantRules: Compiler-owned generated value used to enforce at most one active self contact; applications must not write it.

semantics.purpose: Defines the named groups that organize the user's content catalog.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one content group.
importantRules: Every content item belongs to exactly one content group.
sort_position controls group presentation order without changing stable group identifiers.
semantics.sensitivity: Group names may reveal private content plans and interests.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this content group.
Complete human-facing name of the content group.
Mutable presentation order used to place the group and all of its content in the catalog.
UTC time when this group was removed from active content organization, or null while active.
UTC time when this content group was created.
UTC time of the most recent content-group change, when one has occurred.

semantics.purpose: Catalogs the user's own content and reference material from other creators in one searchable structure.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one work or source item, such as a video, book, article, podcast, image, document, course, or website.
importantRules: Every content item belongs to exactly one content group.
sequence is an optional stable positive number unique within a content group.
relationship_to_user distinguishes the user's authored or planned work from reference material.
transcript preserves source speech or text; personal_notes preserves the user's reaction or intended use.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private drafts, transcripts, reading history, personal notes, and source metadata.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this content item.
Content group that owns and organizes this item.
Stable positive number identifying this content item within its group when numbered organization is used.
importantRules: Unique within content_group_id when present; unlike content_group.sort_position, it identifies an item rather than presentation placement.

semantics.meaning: Action-content format and production surface for this item.

allowedValueMeanings.video_ad: Video advertisement outside the mobile or web UGC-specific formats.
allowedValueMeanings.unknown: Content whose production format has not been identified.

semantics.meaning: Human-readable title of the work or source item.
Source speech or text transcribed or extracted from the content itself.
Summary or description of what the content is about.
UTC publication time reported for the content when known.
Platform or service that hosts the published content.

allowedValueMeanings.none: The content has no external host.

semantics.meaning: Current action-content lifecycle state.

allowedValueMeanings.active: Content is current and available for use.
allowedValueMeanings.obsolete: Content has been superseded and should not guide current work.
allowedValueMeanings.unused: Content is retained but not currently used.
allowedValueMeanings.queued: Content is awaiting production or publication.

semantics.meaning: Canonical public or hosted URL for the content when one exists.
Whether the item is the user's authored or planned work or reference material from elsewhere.

allowedValueMeanings.mine: the user's authored, owned, planned, or produced content.
allowedValueMeanings.reference: Material from another creator kept as a source or reference.

semantics.meaning: Known person, organization, or service that created the content.
the user's own reaction, interpretation, plan, or intended use for the content.
Identifier assigned to the item by its host or source system.
Main locally stored file representing this content item when one exists.
UTC time when the user finished or recorded consuming the reference material.
Ledger event that caused this content item to be created when known.
UTC timestamp when this catalog record was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to this catalog record.
Connects this content item to the contact identified by creator_contact_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each content item may reference zero or one contact; one referenced record may be used by many content item records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this content item to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each content item may reference zero or one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many content item records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this content item to the stored-file record identified by primary_file_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each content item may reference zero or one stored-file record; one referenced record may be used by many content item records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this content item to the content group identified by content_group_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each content item references exactly one content group; one group may contain many content items.
importantRules: A group cannot be deleted while content items still belong to it.

semantics.purpose: Preserves complete logical messages across email, SMS, MMS, iMessage, chat, voicemail, and future communication media.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one inbound, outbound, draft, or internal message, independent of how many participants or files it has.
importantRules: Preserve the complete available message rather than replacing it with extracted facts or a summary.
Use correspondence_participants and correspondence_files for people and attachments.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains highly private communications, message bodies, headers, account identifiers, and provider metadata.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this message.
Communication medium through which the message exists.

allowedValueMeanings.chat: Message from a chat or messaging platform.
allowedValueMeanings.other: Communication medium not covered by the named values.

semantics.meaning: Whether the message arrived, was sent, remains a draft, or exists only as an internal record.

allowedValueMeanings.internal: Recorded for internal agent/user use rather than transmitted.

semantics.meaning: Mailbox, phone identity, or service account through which the message was handled.
Provider or local conversation identifier grouping related messages.
Provider-assigned identifier for this message.
Earlier local correspondence record to which this message directly replies.
Complete message subject or title when the medium provides one.
Complete available plain-text body of the message or voicemail transcript.
Complete available HTML body when supplied by the communication provider.
Provider- or workflow-specific message state, such as unread, sent, failed, or archived.
UTC instant when the message was sent, when known.
UTC instant when the message was received, when known.
Ledger event that introduced or created this correspondence record when known.
UTC timestamp when this local message record was inserted.
Connects this message to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message may reference zero or one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many message records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this message to the message identified by in_reply_to_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message may reference zero or one message; one referenced record may be used by many message records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.purpose: Associates externally stored files with correspondence and identifies how each file appears in the message.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row links one file to one message as an attachment, inline asset, recording, or other file role.
importantRules: The file bytes live in agent media storage; this table stores only the relationship.
semantics.sensitivity: Reveals which private files belong to private communications.

semantics.meaning: Message to which the file belongs.
Externally stored file associated with the message.
How the file appears or functions in the message.

allowedValueMeanings.inline: File displayed inside the message body.
allowedValueMeanings.recording: Audio or video recording that constitutes message content.
allowedValueMeanings.other: File role not covered by the named values.

semantics.meaning: Connects this message-file attachment to the stored-file record identified by file_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message-file attachment references exactly one stored-file record; one referenced record may be used by many message-file attachment records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.meaning: Connects this message-file attachment to the message identified by correspondence_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message-file attachment references exactly one message; one referenced record may be used by many message-file attachment records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.purpose: Records senders and recipients for correspondence while retaining unmatched addresses that do not yet resolve to a contact.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one participant address in one role on one message, optionally linked to a known contact and contact method.
importantRules: address_value preserves the address observed on the message even when no contact matches it.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private communication participants, addresses, and display names.

semantics.meaning: Message on which this participant appears.
Sender or recipient role the observed address has on the message.

allowedValueMeanings.reply_to: Email-style Reply-To address to use when responding instead of the From address.
allowedValueMeanings.sender: Generic sender for media without email-style headers.
allowedValueMeanings.recipient: Generic recipient for media without email-style headers.

semantics.meaning: Known contact matched to the observed participant, when a match exists.
Specific known email address, phone number, or other method matched to the observed participant.
Address or identity exactly observed on the message, retained even when no contact matches.
Participant display name supplied with the message when available.
Connects this message participant to the contact identified by contact_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message participant may reference zero or one contact; one referenced record may be used by many message participant records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this message participant to the message identified by correspondence_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message participant references exactly one message; one referenced record may be used by many message participant records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.meaning: Connects this message participant to the contact method identified by contact_method_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each message participant may reference zero or one contact method; one referenced record may be used by many message participant records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`correspondence_id` AS `correspondence_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`medium` AS `medium`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`direction` AS `direction`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`account_key` AS `account_key`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`thread_key` AS `thread_key`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`external_id` AS `external_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`in_reply_to_id` AS `in_reply_to_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`subject` AS `subject`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`body_text` AS `body_text`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`body_html` AS `body_html`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`status` AS `status`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`sent_at_utc` AS `sent_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`received_at_utc` AS `received_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`source_event_id` AS `source_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`created_at_utc` AS `created_at_utc`,coalesce(`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`received_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`sent_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`.`created_at_utc`) AS `timeline_at_utc` from `chapeauxfous`.`correspondence`

semantics.purpose: Adds one consistently derived timeline timestamp to each correspondence row for chronological message retrieval.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row is one correspondence record with timeline_at_utc chosen from received, sent, or creation time in that order.
importantRules: The view does not duplicate messages; authoritative message data remains in correspondence.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the same highly private communication content as correspondence.

semantics.meaning: Derived chronological timestamp: received_at_utc when present, otherwise sent_at_utc, otherwise created_at_utc.

semantics.purpose: Identifies the application MariaDB database and records its current schema version.
semantics.rowMeaning: The sole row describes the database itself rather than a user-domain entity.
importantRules: The table must contain exactly the singleton row whose key is 1.
schema_version advances only after an approved migration succeeds.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains non-secret internal database metadata.

semantics.meaning: Constant primary key fixed at 1 so the table can contain only one metadata row.
Current integer schema generation expected by the application.
UTC timestamp when this database metadata row was created.
Human-readable description of this database's intended ownership and purpose.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`reminder_id` AS `reminder_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`calendar_event_id` AS `calendar_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`personal_task_id` AS `personal_task_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`title` AS `title`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`remind_at_utc` AS `remind_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`delivery_method` AS `delivery_method`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`delivery_target` AS `delivery_target`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`status` AS `status`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`attempt_count` AS `attempt_count`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`last_attempt_at_utc` AS `last_attempt_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`delivered_at_utc` AS `delivered_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`error_text` AS `error_text`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`created_at_utc` AS `created_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`updated_at_utc` AS `updated_at_utc` from `chapeauxfous`.`reminders` where `chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`status` in ('pending','error') and `chapeauxfous`.`reminders`.`remind_at_utc` <= concat(left(date_format(utc_timestamp(3),'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%i:%s.%f'),23),'Z')

semantics.purpose: Selects reminders that are ready for delivery or retry because their reminder time has arrived and their status is pending or error.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row is one reminder record that is currently due for delivery or retry.
importantRules: This is a time-dependent view; membership changes as the current UTC time and reminder status change.
semantics.sensitivity: May expose private commitments, notification targets, payloads, and delivery errors.

semantics.purpose: Catalogs files held in agent media storage while keeping large binary bytes outside MariaDB.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one externally stored file and records where it is stored plus known integrity and media metadata.
importantRules: storage_path identifies the external bytes; this table never contains the file bytes themselves.
sha256 may be used to verify integrity or identify duplicate content.
semantics.sensitivity: Paths, filenames, hashes, and metadata may reveal private user content even though bytes are stored elsewhere.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this stored-file record.
Unique path locating the file bytes in agent media storage.
Generated SHA-256 digest of storage_path used to enforce uniqueness for externally stored file locations.
importantRules: Compiler-owned generated value; applications must not write it.
semantics.sensitivity: A deterministic digest of a potentially private storage path.

semantics.meaning: Filename supplied by the original source before storage renaming or organization.
Broad media category used by agent workflows.

allowedValueMeanings.archive: Archive containing one or more files.
allowedValueMeanings.other: File type not covered by the named media categories.

semantics.meaning: Internet media type reported or detected for the file.
SHA-256 digest of the file bytes for integrity verification and duplicate detection.
Size of the stored file in bytes.
Playback duration of audio or video in milliseconds when known.
Pixel width of an image or video when known.
Pixel height of an image or video when known.
Stable event_id of the ledger event that introduced the file when known.
UTC timestamp when this file metadata record was inserted.
Concise human-facing title for the stored file. Initially derived from the original filename and may later be suggested by AI or edited by the user.
Plain-language searchable description of the file contents.
Authority that supplied the current title, used to prevent AI from overwriting a user-edited title.

allowedValueMeanings.original_filename: The title is the deterministic upload-time fallback.
allowedValueMeanings.ai: The title was suggested by the model after inspecting the file.
allowedValueMeanings.user: The title was confirmed or edited by the user and must not be overwritten by AI.

semantics.meaning: UTC timestamp of the most recent title or description change.

semantics.purpose: Stores each reusable exchange's literal opening, authoritative structured contract, current answers, and resumable progress.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row is one complete numbered interaction step and its mutable current-run state.
importantRules: The parent interaction_guides.version is the only definition concurrency version and increments when any exchange definition changes.
The contract's structured inputs, operations, recovery reads, and completion rule are authoritative; explanatory instructions cannot introduce undeclared behavior.
A run remains on its current exchange until the contract completion rule is satisfied, then advances to the next higher enabled number.
Completing a run preserves its progress in activity_events, then immediately resets answers_json and progress_state for the next run.
Generic database reads and writes must not expose or mutate these private rows; use the owning interaction-guide tools.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private scripted openings, reusable execution contracts, and the user's current answers.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for one numbered interaction-guide step.
Identifier of the parent interaction guide that owns this step and its definition version.
Positive user-facing number ordering this step within its guide.
importantRules: Numbers may contain gaps; completion advances to the next higher enabled number rather than assuming current plus one.

semantics.meaning: Fixed opening text that begins this step every time it becomes current.
importantRules: Present this text literally rather than asking the model to paraphrase it.

semantics.meaning: Versioned JSON contract containing optional explanatory instructions plus authoritative typed inputs, exact destination operations and argument bindings, bounded recovery reads, and the completion rule.
semantics.format: JSON object, contract version 1, at most 200000 characters
importantRules: Free-text instructions may explain structured fields but cannot introduce undeclared inputs, tools, destinations, recovery actions, or completion requirements.
Every destination mutation names its exact application tool and argument template in operations.
The completion mode is contract data, not a separate exchange column.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private workflow instructions and destination identifiers.

semantics.meaning: JSON object containing answers the user has actually supplied for this step in the current run, keyed by concise stable answer names.
importantRules: Merge partial answers without discarding answers already collected in the active run.
A completed run clears this object only after that run's progress has been retained in activity_events.
Answers do not replace business validation or successful receipts from the tools that own destination data.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private user answers that may span any domain covered by the structured interaction.

semantics.meaning: Whether new and active runs include this step when selecting the current and next higher numbered step.

allowedValueMeanings.0: The definition is retained but skipped by runs.

semantics.meaning: UTC timestamp when this numbered interaction-guide step was created.
UTC timestamp of the most recent definition or current-answer update to this step, when one has occurred.
Current-run progress for this step, used to resume an interrupted structured interaction at exactly one active step.

allowedValueMeanings.pending: The current run has not yet completed this step.
allowedValueMeanings.active: This is the current step to present or continue.
allowedValueMeanings.completed: The current run completed this step and advanced beyond it.

importantRules: The interaction-guide service owns transitions; definition tools do not write this field directly.
Run completion or explicit cancellation resets current progress only after immutable history is retained in activity_events.

semantics.meaning: Each numbered step belongs to exactly one interaction guide; deleting a guide deletes its child step definitions.
semantics.cardinality: many interaction_guide_steps to one interaction_guides
importantRules: Definition tools update the parent guide version in the same transaction as a child step change.

semantics.purpose: Stores named, versioned containers for durable user-owned structured interactions.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one named interaction guide whose complete interaction content is defined by its numbered steps.
importantRules: Numbered steps are loaded only when the user explicitly asks to use, inspect, or change that exact guide.
A guide describes an interaction but does not own a schedule or recurrence.
A repeating to-do may reference a guide through todo_routines.interaction_guide_id.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private preferences, questions, and instructions for the user's personal interactions with the agent.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for one interaction guide.
User-facing unique name used to select the guide without loading its text.
importantRules: Names are unique without regard to letter case.

semantics.meaning: Lifecycle state controlling whether the guide is available for new guided interactions.

allowedValueMeanings.active: The guide is available to inspect, edit, start, and link from a repeating to-do.
allowedValueMeanings.archived: The guide is retained as history but unavailable for new links or starts.

semantics.meaning: Monotonically increasing optimistic-concurrency version for agent and UI edits.
importantRules: An update or archive must match the current version and increments it on success.

semantics.meaning: UTC timestamp when the interaction guide was created.
UTC timestamp of the most recent successful guide update or archival, when one has occurred.

semantics.purpose: Stores the user's authoritative time-stamped personal observations under reusable trackers.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one complete personal observation with an optional numeric projection in its tracker's canonical unit.
importantRules: content_text is the complete human-readable observation; number_value is an optional trend projection rather than a replacement for it.
occurred_at_utc records when the observed event happened, while created_at_utc records when the row was saved.
The parent tracker owns the single canonical unit for every number_value in its series; entries never duplicate a unit.
For imported rows, the source and non-null external_id pair is a stable idempotency key and must never identify two different observations.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private personal observations that may include health, nutrition, habits, symptoms, and daily activities.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for one personal log entry.
Tracker under which this observation is recorded.
UTC instant when the logged observation or event occurred.
importantRules: This may differ from created_at_utc when the user logs something retrospectively.

semantics.meaning: Complete self-contained natural-language content of the observation.
importantRules: Preserve supporting context here instead of fragmenting it into a separate note field.
When a numeric projection exists, this text still remains the complete readable entry.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private health, nutrition, behavioral, or situational context.

semantics.meaning: Optional numeric projection extracted from the complete log content for calculation, comparison, and trends.
importantRules: Null is valid for observations without a useful numeric component.
Interpret this value using the parent tracker's canonical unit.

semantics.meaning: Optional activity event for the user request that caused this log entry to be recorded.
UTC timestamp when this log row was created.
UTC timestamp of the most recent modification to this log row, when modified.
Stable generic name of the application, export, or local path from which this log entry originated.
importantRules: Use agent-slayer for ordinary native log writes and a consistent source name for every page of one external import.
semantics.sensitivity: May identify a private external application or data export.

semantics.meaning: Optional stable record identifier assigned by source and used with source to make imports idempotent.
importantRules: Required by the generic import tool and null for ordinary native logs without an upstream identity.
The pair of source and external_id is unique whenever external_id is present.
semantics.sensitivity: May expose an identifier from a private external data source.

semantics.meaning: Connects this log entry to the observable request event that created it.
semantics.cardinality: Each log entry may reference zero or one activity event; one activity event may create multiple log entries.
importantRules: Deleting the source event preserves the log entry and clears this reference.

semantics.meaning: Connects this observation to the reusable tracker that gives it identity and organization.
semantics.cardinality: Each log entry belongs to exactly one tracker; one tracker may contain many log entries.
importantRules: A tracker with historical entries cannot be deleted through this restricted relationship.

semantics.purpose: Defines broad named groups that organize the user's personal trackers.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one organizational group such as Health, Home, or General.
importantRules: Groups organize trackers but do not identify individual observations.
Group names are unique without regard to letter case.
semantics.sensitivity: Group names may reveal private areas of the user's life and health.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for one personal-log group.
Complete human-facing name of the group.
importantRules: Unique without regard to letter case.
semantics.sensitivity: May identify a private area of activity or health.

semantics.meaning: UTC timestamp when this group was archived, or null while it is active.
UTC timestamp when this group was created.
UTC timestamp of the most recent change to this group, when changed.

semantics.purpose: Stores deliberate personal notes, journal entries, ideas, and reference notes independently of conversational history.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one complete note, optionally attached to another agent record and traced to the event that created it.
importantRules: Preserve the useful original note text in body_text rather than reducing it to extracted fragments.
subject_type and subject_id are a polymorphic pair and should be set together.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private personal writing, journal content, ideas, and contextual links.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this note.
Optional concise human-readable title for the note.
Complete substantive text of the note.
Kind of note based on the user's intent for the writing.

allowedValueMeanings.other: Note intent not covered by the named values.

semantics.meaning: Current retention and visibility state of the note.

allowedValueMeanings.archived: Retained but removed from active notes.
allowedValueMeanings.deleted: Soft-deleted and normally excluded from use.

semantics.meaning: Type of record this note concerns, used together with subject_id.
Identifier of the record named by subject_type.
Ledger event containing the interaction or observation from which the note was created when known.
UTC time the note is about when that differs from when the note was stored.
UTC timestamp when the note was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to the note.
Connects this note to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each note may reference zero or one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many note records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`personal_task_id` AS `personal_task_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`todo_group_id` AS `todo_group_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`todo_routine_id` AS `todo_routine_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`sequence` AS `sequence`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`related_contact_id` AS `related_contact_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`text` AS `text`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`status` AS `status`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`sort_position` AS `sort_position`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`scheduled_at_utc` AS `scheduled_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`due_at_utc` AS `due_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`completed_at_utc` AS `completed_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`source` AS `source`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`external_id` AS `external_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`source_event_id` AS `source_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`created_at_utc` AS `created_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`updated_at_utc` AS `updated_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`is_all_day` AS `is_all_day`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`duration_minutes` AS `duration_minutes`,`chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`planning_prompt_text` AS `planning_prompt_text` from `chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal` where `chapeauxfous`.`todo_personal`.`status` in ('unplanned','todo','ai_suggested')

semantics.purpose: Provides the personal tasks that currently belong on the user's actionable To-Do List.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one task whose status is unplanned, todo, or ai_suggested.
importantRules: The view includes unplanned, todo, and ai_suggested tasks and excludes complete, ignored, and archived tasks.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the user's private plans, commitments, and agent-suggested work.

semantics.purpose: Stores the current and archived durable facts and preferences that describe the user to the secretary.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one version of one self-contained typed profile fact; multiple active rows may share a fact type.
importantRules: Only active rows of repository-selected relevant fact types are included automatically in first-call model context.
A type is a broad repeatable category; the text identifies the person or item to which each row applies.
Replacing a fact targets its exact profile_fact_id, archives that row, and inserts a new active version.
Deleting a fact targets its exact profile_fact_id and archives it rather than erasing historical data.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private user identity, location, address, preferences, and other durable personal information.

semantics.meaning: Stable row identifier used by profile tools to replace or archive this exact fact.
Broad repeatable category for this fact, shared by related rows when appropriate.
importantRules: Multiple active rows may have the same fact_type.

semantics.meaning: Self-contained natural-language statement identifying the fact's person or item.
examples: My car is a 2017 Volkswagen Golf.
My wife's car is a 2020 Honda CR-V.
My son Vince's shoe size is 9 US.
importantRules: The text must remain understandable without deriving a subject from fact_type.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private personal information.

semantics.meaning: Whether the fact is current or retained only as archived history.

allowedValueMeanings.active: Current fact eligible for first-call context when its type is relevant.
allowedValueMeanings.archived: Historical fact omitted from ordinary model context.

semantics.meaning: User request event that created this version of the fact.
User request event that archived this fact version, either by replacement or deletion.
UTC time when this fact version was created.
UTC time when the fact was most recently changed.
UTC time when the fact was archived; null while active.
Connects an archived fact version to the request that replaced or deleted it.
semantics.cardinality: Each archived fact version may reference zero or one archiving event; one event may archive multiple fact versions.
importantRules: Deleting an old event clears this pointer without deleting the profile fact version.

semantics.meaning: Connects the fact version to the request that created it.
semantics.cardinality: Each profile fact version may reference zero or one source event; one event may create multiple profile fact versions.
importantRules: Deleting an old event clears this pointer without deleting the profile fact.

semantics.purpose: Represents directed relationships between arbitrary agent records when adding a dedicated foreign-key column would be excessive.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row states that one typed record has one named relationship to another typed record.
importantRules: Direction matters: left and right records are not interchangeable unless the relationship type explicitly says so.
The text identifiers are polymorphic and are not enforced by MariaDB foreign keys.
semantics.sensitivity: May reveal private relationships among contacts, notes, content, work, and events.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this directed record relationship.
Type of record from whose perspective relationship_type is stated.
Text representation of the identifier for the record named by left_record_type.
Directional phrase describing how the left record relates to the right record.
Type of record that is the target of the relationship.
Text representation of the identifier for the record named by right_record_type.
Free-text qualification or evidence needed to understand the relationship.
Ledger event from which this relationship was learned or requested when known.
UTC timestamp when this record relationship was inserted.
Connects this directed record relationship to the observable event identified by source_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each directed record relationship may reference zero or one observable event; one referenced record may be used by many directed record relationship records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row preserves this row and clears the reference.

semantics.purpose: Assigns reusable tags to arbitrary typed records without requiring a separate join table for every record type.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row assigns one tag to one typed record.
importantRules: record_type and record_id form a polymorphic reference that MariaDB cannot validate with a foreign key.
semantics.sensitivity: Tag assignments may reveal private categorization of people, communications, work, or content.

semantics.meaning: Tag assigned to the record.
Type of record receiving the tag.
Text representation of the identifier for the record named by record_type.
UTC timestamp when the tag was assigned.
Connects this tag assignment to the tag identified by tag_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each tag assignment references exactly one tag; one referenced record may be used by many tag assignment records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.purpose: Stores when and how an alarm should be delivered and preserves observable delivery, retry, and error state.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one standalone, calendar-linked, or personal-task-linked reminder and its delivery lifecycle.
importantRules: A reminder may link to a calendar event, a personal task, or neither.
Delivery attempts must update attempt_count and the corresponding timing or error fields.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private reminder text, linked commitments, delivery targets, payloads, and errors.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this reminder.
Calendar event whose timing or commitment this reminder supports, when applicable.
Optional personal task whose reminder lifecycle this row serves.
importantRules: Deleting the task also deletes its subordinate reminder.

semantics.meaning: Human-readable notification text or reminder name.
UTC instant at or after which the reminder becomes due for delivery.
Mechanism through which the reminder should be delivered.

allowedValueMeanings.agent: Agent surfaces the reminder through its normal interaction channel.
allowedValueMeanings.other: Delivery mechanism not covered by the named values.

semantics.meaning: Method-specific destination such as an address, number, endpoint, or device when needed.
Current delivery lifecycle state of the reminder.

allowedValueMeanings.pending: Waiting for remind_at_utc or delivery processing.
allowedValueMeanings.snoozed: Delivery was postponed to a later time.
allowedValueMeanings.error: Most recent delivery attempt failed and may need retry or correction.

semantics.meaning: Number of delivery attempts already made.
UTC time of the most recent delivery attempt.
UTC time successful delivery was recorded.
Most recent observable delivery error when status is error.
UTC timestamp when the reminder was inserted.
UTC timestamp of the latest recorded change to the reminder.
Connects this reminder to the calendar event identified by calendar_event_id.
semantics.cardinality: Each reminder may reference zero or one calendar event; one referenced record may be used by many reminder records.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced row also deletes this dependent row.

semantics.meaning: Connects a reminder to the optional personal task occurrence it is intended to surface.
semantics.cardinality: Each reminder may reference zero or one personal task; one task may have multiple reminders.
importantRules: Deleting the referenced task also deletes its dependent reminder.

semantics.purpose: Defines reusable human labels that can categorize many kinds of agent records.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row defines one tag with a stable machine slug and human-facing label.
importantRules: Use slug for stable matching and label for display.
Inactive tags remain defined but should not normally be offered for new assignments.
semantics.sensitivity: Tag names may reveal private organizational categories.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for this tag.
Unique stable machine identifier used for matching and references.
Human-readable text displayed for the tag.
1 when the tag is available for normal use; otherwise 0.
UTC timestamp when the tag was defined.

semantics.purpose: Defines the named groups that organize the user's one authoritative personal To-Do List.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one named task group, such as Inbox or Watches.
importantRules: Groups are named containers, not tasks and not a second hierarchy.
Group names are unique without regard to letter case.
When uses_sequence is 1, a newly inserted task with no sequence receives max(sequence) + 1 within this group; when it is 0, sequence remains optional.
semantics.sensitivity: Group names may reveal the user's private projects and areas of responsibility.

semantics.meaning: Stable internal identifier for one personal to-do group.
Complete human-facing name of the group; the schema intentionally has no separate description.
importantRules: Unique without regard to letter case.
semantics.sensitivity: May identify a private project or area of responsibility.

semantics.meaning: UTC instant when the group was archived; null while the group is active.
UTC instant when the group record was created.
UTC instant of the group record’s most recent material update; null until first updated.
Mutable presentation order used to place this group and all of its tasks in the to-do list.
importantRules: Lower values appear first; moving a group does not change task membership or task order within the group.

semantics.meaning: Whether this group automatically assigns the next unique positive sequence number to tasks added without one.

allowedValueMeanings.0: Sequence numbers are optional and are not assigned automatically.
allowedValueMeanings.1: Unnumbered tasks receive the next number after the group's current maximum.

importantRules: Disabling automatic sequencing preserves numbers already assigned.

semantics.purpose: Stores actual actionable and historical occurrences in the user’s authoritative personal To-Do List.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one actual personal task occurrence; todo_routine_id optionally links it to the reusable definition that produced it.
importantRules: Every task belongs to exactly one todo group.
sequence is an optional stable identifier unique within a group; sort_position is mutable presentation order.
scheduled_at_utc places work on the calendar, due_at_utc is its deadline, and completed_at_utc records actual completion.
The single text field contains the concrete plan for this occurrence and may differ from its parent routine text.
Editing an occurrence does not rewrite its linked routine definition.
unplanned is an active status for an item that still needs a concrete plan.
planning_prompt_text is nullable and independent of status.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the user's private tasks, plans, relationships, schedules, and source references.

semantics.meaning: Stable internal identifier for one personal task.
Required group that contains and orders this personal task.
Optional parent routine definition that generated this actual task occurrence.
Stable positive number that identifies this task within its group when that group uses numbered work.
importantRules: Unique within todo_group_id when present; unlike sort_position, it does not change when the list is reordered.

semantics.meaning: Optional contact that this task concerns; it does not assign ownership of the task.
Complete wording of the task, serving as both its short label and any longer explanation.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private plans, names, and instructions.

semantics.meaning: Compact lifecycle state controlling whether and how the task appears in the user's list.

allowedValueMeanings.unplanned: The item is active but still needs a concrete plan.
allowedValueMeanings.todo: the user intends to do this task.
allowedValueMeanings.ignore: The task was intentionally skipped without completion.
allowedValueMeanings.archive: The task is retained as history but removed from ordinary views.
allowedValueMeanings.ai_suggested: The agent proposed the task and the user has not yet accepted or dismissed it.

semantics.meaning: Mutable ordering value used to place tasks directly within a group; it conveys no importance or priority.
importantRules: Lower values appear first within the same group.

semantics.meaning: UTC instant when the user intends to work on the task; this projects the task onto the calendar.
UTC deadline by which the task should be complete, distinct from its scheduled work time.
UTC instant when the task entered complete status; null for tasks not currently complete.
Optional stable name of the system or workflow that supplied this task.
Optional identifier assigned by source; together with source it prevents duplicate imports or publications.
importantRules: Unique with source when both values are present.

semantics.meaning: Optional observable activity event that created or imported this task.
UTC instant when this task occurrence was created.
UTC instant of this task occurrence’s most recent material update; null until first updated.
1 when the task is assigned to its scheduled calendar date without an exact clock time; otherwise 0.
Optional positive planned duration for this task occurrence.
Optional question the agent should proactively ask to help turn this task into a concrete plan.
examples: What do we want to do while we have the kids this afternoon?
importantRules: Null means the task has no stored planning question.
The field may be present on any task status and does not itself change the status.

semantics.meaning: Associates a personal task with the optional contact it concerns without assigning task ownership.
semantics.cardinality: Each task references zero or one contact; one contact may be referenced by multiple tasks.
importantRules: Deleting a contact preserves the task and clears this optional reference.

semantics.meaning: Places each personal task in its required to-do group.
semantics.cardinality: Each task belongs to exactly one group; one group may contain multiple tasks.
importantRules: A group cannot be deleted while tasks still belong to it.

semantics.meaning: Links an actual personal task occurrence to the optional reusable routine definition that generated it.
semantics.cardinality: Each task references zero or one routine; one routine may generate multiple task occurrences.
importantRules: Deleting a routine preserves generated task history and clears this optional reference.

semantics.meaning: Links a personal task to the optional observable activity event that created or imported it.
semantics.cardinality: Each task references zero or one source event; one event may create multiple tasks.
importantRules: Deleting an activity event preserves the task and clears this optional reference.

semantics.purpose: Stores authoritative reusable definitions for standing calendar routines and completion-driven recurring personal tasks.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one reusable routine definition, including its publication behavior, destination group, default occurrence content, schedule anchor, and recurrence rule.
importantRules: A calendar routine is a definition, not a hidden personal task; publishing creates dated tasks linked by todo_routine_id.
An on_completion routine generates its next actual task when the current linked occurrence is completed or ignored.
Editing a linked task occurrence does not rewrite the parent routine definition.
RRULE determines recurrence from first_scheduled_at_utc in time_zone.
Default status, contact, duration, guide, and planning prompt are copied into newly generated occurrences.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains the user's private recurring responsibilities and schedules.

semantics.meaning: Stable internal identifier for one reusable to-do routine definition.
Required destination group for task occurrences generated from this routine.
Controls whether dated occurrences are published into calendar ranges or generated after completion of the prior occurrence.
Complete wording copied into every generated task occurrence; there is no title-description split.
semantics.sensitivity: May contain private recurring plans and instructions.

semantics.meaning: Initial lifecycle status assigned to each new task occurrence.
UTC instant anchoring the RRULE and the first scheduled task occurrence.
Optional first deadline; its offset from first_scheduled_at_utc is preserved for generated occurrences.
IANA time-zone name used to preserve local wall-clock recurrence across daylight-saving changes.
RFC 5545 RRULE that defines daily, day-of-week, monthly, quarterly, or other recurrence.
semantics.format: RFC 5545 RRULE without a required RRULE: prefix

semantics.meaning: Optional contact copied to each newly generated task occurrence.
Positive planned duration copied to each task occurrence.
UTC instant when this routine stopped generating new occurrences; null while enabled.
Activity event that created this routine definition.
UTC instant when this routine definition was created.
UTC instant of this routine definition’s most recent material update; null until first updated.
Optional interaction guide offered when the user starts an occurrence of this recurring to-do.
importantRules: This reference does not schedule or repeat the guide; the containing to-do routine owns recurrence.

semantics.meaning: Optional proactive planning question copied into each task occurrence generated from this routine.
examples: What would make family time fun this weekend?
importantRules: Null means generated occurrences have no routine-supplied planning question.

semantics.meaning: Associates a routine definition with the optional contact copied to each new task occurrence.
semantics.cardinality: Each routine references zero or one contact; one contact may be referenced by multiple routines.
importantRules: Deleting a contact clears this optional reference without deleting the routine.

semantics.meaning: Places each routine definition in the required destination group for its generated task occurrences.
semantics.cardinality: Each routine belongs to exactly one group; one group may contain multiple routines.
importantRules: A group cannot be deleted while routine definitions still reference it.

semantics.meaning: Associates a recurring to-do definition with the optional interaction guide offered by each generated task occurrence.
semantics.cardinality: Each recurring to-do references zero or one interaction guide; one guide may be referenced by multiple recurring to-dos.
importantRules: Deleting a guide clears this optional reference without deleting the recurring to-do.

semantics.meaning: Links the routine definition to the activity event that created it.
semantics.cardinality: Each routine references zero or one source event.

semantics.purpose: Defines the reusable subjects under which the user records personal observations over time.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one globally named tracked subject, such as Weight, Bowel movement, Mood, or Medication.
importantRules: Tracker names are globally unique without regard to letter case so a natural-language log request has one unambiguous target.
Every tracker has one canonical unit shared by its complete numeric series.
The migration marker set me must be replaced before another entry is recorded.
A canonical unit cannot be changed after numeric entries exist, except when replacing the set me migration marker.
semantics.sensitivity: Tracker names may reveal private health conditions, habits, medications, or other personal interests.

semantics.meaning: Stable local identifier for one personal tracker.
Organizational group containing this tracker.
Complete human-facing name of the tracked subject.
importantRules: Unique globally without regard to letter case.
semantics.sensitivity: May name a private health condition, habit, medication, or activity.

semantics.meaning: Canonical unit shared by every numeric entry in this tracker's trend series.
importantRules: Required for every tracker; event-style trackers use an explicit count such as occurrence or dose.
The set me value is a migration review marker, not a real measurement unit.
After numeric entries exist, changing this unit would reinterpret history and is rejected unless the old value is set me.

semantics.meaning: UTC timestamp when tracking was archived, or null while the tracker is active.
UTC timestamp when this tracker was first defined.
UTC timestamp of the most recent change to this tracker, when changed.
Connects this tracker to the group that organizes it.
semantics.cardinality: Each tracker belongs to exactly one log group; one log group may contain many trackers.
importantRules: A group containing trackers cannot be deleted through this restricted relationship.

mechanics.definition: select `chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`calendar_event_id` AS `calendar_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`ical_uid` AS `ical_uid`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`ical_recurrence_id` AS `ical_recurrence_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`title` AS `title`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`description` AS `description`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`location_text` AS `location_text`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`starts_at_utc` AS `starts_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`ends_at_utc` AS `ends_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`time_zone` AS `time_zone`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`is_all_day` AS `is_all_day`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`status` AS `status`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`recurrence_rule` AS `recurrence_rule`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`source_event_id` AS `source_event_id`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`created_at_utc` AS `created_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`updated_at_utc` AS `updated_at_utc`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`planning_prompt_text` AS `planning_prompt_text`,`chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`ical_single_guard` AS `ical_single_guard` from `chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events` where `chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`status` in ('tentative','confirmed') and `chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`starts_at_utc` >= concat(left(date_format(utc_timestamp(3),'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%i:%s.%f'),23),'Z') order by `chapeauxfous`.`calendar_events`.`starts_at_utc`

semantics.purpose: Selects tentative and confirmed calendar events whose start time has not yet passed, ordered by start time.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one tentative or confirmed calendar event whose start time has not yet passed.
importantRules: This is a time-dependent view and excludes cancelled, completed, and already-started events.
semantics.sensitivity: Contains private future schedule and location information.

semantics.purpose: Tracks background execution attempts for script-driven video productions and any retained legacy render jobs.
semantics.rowMeaning: One row represents one attempt to render one video using one renderer, template, input package, and eventual output or error.
importantRules: A script-driven video job is subordinate execution state and never replaces its authoritative video_scripts record.
At most one queued, preparing, or rendering job may exist for one linked script.
